exposure: timing of epidural analgesia initiation (cervical dilation <5 cm vs >=5 cm)
cohort: 297 primiparous women with singleton term pregnancies (37-42 weeks of gestation) who received epidural analgesia for labor.
finding: Late epidural analgesia administered at cervical dilation >=5 cm was associated with a shorter active phase of the first stage of labor and a lower cesarean delivery rate without increasing adverse maternal or neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Late epidural analgesia (at cervical dilation >=5 cm) was associated with a lower cesarean delivery rate.
